situation (example wording): "what is NIBRS", "what data do you have", "where does this data come from", "what is Homicide Reports"
what the app does today: Describes a source in free wording that changes from one answer to the next.
proposed behavior: A question about what a source is gives one fixed text for that source, flat and factual (who reports, years covered, what is left out), with no marketing tone and no wording that changes between answers. The bracketed items are filled by the release at run time: [most recent year], [most recent month], [last month] and [last year] are the latest year or month the data hold, so the text stays true after each monthly update. The texts are: Crime Index - Historical: "Crime Index - Historical holds yearly counts of crimes, law enforcement staffing, and clearances. Police agencies report the figures to the FBI. It has no detail on victims, offenders or weapons, and it has no monthly counts. Crime and staffing data for many agencies is available from 1930 to [most recent year] while state and national estimates are available from 1960 on." Crime Index - Current: "Crime Index - Current holds monthly counts of crime and clearances from 2017 to [most recent month] for city agencies of 50,000 or more and county agencies of 100,000 or more. Police agencies report these preliminary figures which give an approximate of national crime trends. It has no detail on victims, offenders or weapons." NIBRS: "NIBRS is the FBI's National Incident-Based Reporting System. Police agencies report each crime incident to the FBI: the offenses, victims, offenders, weapons, arrests and clearances. The data here run by month from 1991 for some agencies through [most recent month]. It covers only agencies that report through NIBRS, so a state or year can have few agencies or none. It leaves out crimes not reported to police." Homicide Reports: "Homicide Reports comes from the FBI's Supplementary Homicide Reports. Police agencies report data on murders to the FBI with details of the victim, the offender, the weapon and the circumstances. The data here run from 1985 through [last month]. It covers murder and non-negligent manslaughter only. It leaves out agencies that did not report in a year, and it has no other crimes." Hate crimes: "Hate crime data come from FBI Hate Crime Statistics. Police agencies report to the FBI the incidents they classify as motivated by bias, with the bias type, the offense and the location. The data run from 1991 through [last year]. Reporting is voluntary, so agencies that did not report are missing. Incidents not reported to police or not classified as bias-motivated are left out." Each source tab (Crime Index - Historical, Crime Index - Current, NIBRS, Homicide Reports, Hate crimes) returns only its own text.
exact default or choices offered: The fixed text for the source asked about, word for word with the bracketed items filled, and nothing else added.
why: Jeff 2026-11-22 (card through the coordinator): a bland definition of the source, one fixed text per source; he edited the wording of the texts.
status: Decided 2026-11-22 (Jeff, through the coordinator); build: Engine
test cases: Questions of the form "what is <source>" for each source return its fixed text (expected values to be set from the build).
